report.source_text: Computed tomography of thorax showed few well defined heterogeneously enhancing masses nearly occupying whole of bilateral hemithorax. The masses were showing heterogeneously enhancing soft tissue component with intermixed areas of necrosis. No evidence of calcification were seen within the masses. The masses were displacing the heart and great vessels anteriorly with stretching of left pulmonary vein. Right pulmonary vein was not visualized. Trachea was displaced towards right side with severe compression over esophagus. The largest mass on the right side was measuring ∼ 110 × 100 × 170 mm predominantly involving the right middle and lower lobes with partial collapse of right upper lobe. The mass was indenting on the right hemi diaphragm, displacing the liver inferiorly. A similar mass measuring ∼ 44 × 40 × 35 mm was seen in apical segment of right upper lobe. The largest mass on the left measures 110 × 90 × 140 mm and was predominantly involving anteromedial and lateral segment of left lower lobe. Two similar other masses were seen measuring ∼ 65 × 53 × 45 mm (in the left upper lobe) and 30 × 31 × 32 mm (in the lateral basal segment of left lower lobe). Pleural effusion or mediastinal lymphadenopathy were not evident.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 27-year-old male presented with dry cough, chest tightness, and difficulty breathing. Initial CT thorax revealed multiple large, heterogeneously enhancing masses in both lungs with areas of necrosis, displacing surrounding structures. Biopsy showed sheets and fascicles of spindle-shaped cells. Immunohistochemistry was positive for TLE-1, CD56, CD99, and Bcl2, and negative for Pan CK, NKX-2.2, and EMA, strongly suggesting synovial sarcoma. PET-CT confirmed metabolic activity in one of the masses. Molecular testing for SYT-SSX translocation was not documented.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with respiratory symptoms including dry cough, chest tightness, and difficulty breathing.

CT thorax revealed multiple large, heterogeneously enhancing masses in both hemithoraces with areas of necrosis, displacing surrounding structures, and no calcification, pleural effusion, or mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
Biopsy showed sheets and fascicles of spindle-shaped cells with vesicular nuclei, dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and moderate pale cytoplasm, with few mitoses.
Immunohistochemistry was positive for TLE-1, CD56, CD99, and Bcl2, and negative for Pan CK, NKX-2.2, and EMA, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of 10-12%.
PET-CT showed heterogeneously increased FDG uptake (SUV max 8.09) in a mass.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Sputum examination for tuberculosis was negative.
Immunohistochemistry was negative for Pan CK.

remaining_uncertainties: Molecular confirmation of SYT-SSX translocation was not documented.
Details of treatment initiated and patient's response or clinical outcome are not documented.
The exact temporal relationship and distinctness of findings across the different imaging reports (E001, E003, E004) are not fully clarified, though all point to multiple lung masses.
